name: sni-drop
description: A TLS ClientHello naming the relay's cover host is swallowed, and so is every later client packet of that flow — no RST, no ICMP: the TCP connection opens and then the handshake simply never completes. The box reassembles a ClientHello that spans TCP segments. Only the family that sends that name is blocked.
analogue: In-path drop on a TLS trigger: the GFW's ESNI blocking (since July 2020: 'drop all client-to-server packets') and its fully-encrypted-traffic blocker, both silent; and what happens when a cover SNI itself lands on a blocklist (XTLS #3269). Model: exact server_name match, per-flow. It does NOT model residual blocking of the 3-tuple for 120-180 s after the trigger, record-layer fragmentation (a ClientHello split across TLS records is not parsed — the real blind spot too), or ECH.
